images.title: Add the two before
images.purpose: Show that in 3, 4, 7, 11, 18 each term is the sum of the two terms before it, so the next is 29.
images.composition: One row of boxes with one highlighted sum below, centred.
images.exact_structure: Six equal boxes in a row, evenly spaced: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18 in teal #0072B2 and a dashed grey #6B7280 sixth box holding 29 in amber #E69F00. Under the row, centred, one grey #6B7280 bracket spans the boxes 11 and 18 and points to the sixth box. Exactly 6 boxes, 1 bracket, 1 equation.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a bracket over more than two boxes
images.takeaway: Each term is the sum of the two terms just before it.
images.description: Boxes 3, 4, 7, 11, 18 with a bracket over 11 and 18 leading to 29.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to add the two boxes under the bracket and match the result to the dashed box.

image_decisions.why: One bracket on the last two terms carries the rule without cluttering the row.
